note: Free options verified on the date shown from each provider's own pages. Free tiers change often: check the source link before relying on a limit.
safety: Never paste passwords, API keys, tokens, .env files or private keys into any AI tool.
Free cloud tiers may use what you send to improve or train their models. Keep customer and personal data out unless you use a local model.
Check facts, links and numbers before you rely on them: AI tools can sound confident and still be wrong.
Check the terms before using AI output commercially, especially images.

providers.name: Gemini app
providers.free: Free plan ($0 with a Google Account): the Flash-Lite model, image creation and editing, Deep Research and Canvas.
providers.privacy: A cloud chat app: what you type is sent to Google. Check the app's activity and privacy settings before sharing anything sensitive.

providers.name: Google AI Studio
providers.free: Gemini API free tier: free input and output tokens for models such as Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemma 4, with rate limits. Long documents fit well.
providers.privacy: Google's pricing page says free-tier content is used to improve its products. Use the paid tier or a local model for anything private.

providers.name: ChatGPT Free
providers.free: Free plan: everyday chats, with limits on uploads, image creation, voice and deep research.
providers.privacy: OpenAI's pricing page says Free plan content is used to train its models, with an opt-out available in settings.

providers.name: Mistral Vibe (was Le Chat)
providers.free: Free plan: limited messages and web searches, basic image generation and editing. Le Chat became Vibe in May 2026.
providers.privacy: Mistral's pricing page lists a training opt-out for paid plans but doesn't say how the Free plan is handled. Assume it may be used and keep secrets out.

providers.name: Ollama (on your computer)
providers.free: Running open models on your own computer is free and unlimited: Qwen, Llama, Gemma, Mistral, DeepSeek and many more. TribeCode's local brain can use it too.
providers.privacy: Local models run on your machine, so prompts stay with you. Ollama's optional cloud models are paid and run on its servers.

providers.name: LM Studio (on your computer)
providers.free: Free plan ($0): download and run local models with llama.cpp and MLX in a desktop app. For work use, check LM Studio's terms.
providers.privacy: Runs on your own computer, so prompts stay local.

providers.name: OpenRouter free models
providers.free: Models marked ":free": 20 requests a minute and 50 a day (1,000 a day once you have bought at least 10 credits). The free list changes often.
providers.privacy: Free models are served by different providers with different data policies, and some may log prompts. Check the model's page first.

providers.name: GroqCloud
providers.free: Groq's rate-limit docs list free-plan limits, for example 30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day for gpt-oss-120b. Your console shows your exact limits.
providers.privacy: A cloud API: prompts are sent to Groq. Read its data policy before sending anything private.
